incident-bot: :warning: realtime-regression-detector alert for service=redwood-stream route=/v1/stream generate_type=chat region=eu-west-1

incident-bot: signals -> p95=2.34s (baseline 0.25s), p99=7.10s (baseline 0.55s), streaming stalls at tail, consumer-latency spikes; autoscaler activity low; error-rate +0.1pp

jules: I'm on call. seeing alert, opening thread. dashboards show an abrupt step around 1766668940.

rachel: any recent config or deploys? I pushed a tiny runtime flag earlier but it was scoped to staging only.

anand: infra-bot shows a kernel-driver update on 3 hosts in eu-west-1 at 1766668800 (driver v2.14 -> v2.15). could that affect GPU kernel compile times?

tom: tailing runtime logs on affected pods:
```
[ERROR] gpu-kernel: jit-compile-failed, fallback-emu, t=950ms
[WARN] kvcache: eviction-churn, evict-count=4200, avg-latency=1100ms
[INFO] stream: token-flush=2800ms client-wait=3100ms
```

maya: network-wise, no LB config changes. Router shows increased connection queuing for the stream tier. backend queue length jumped from 5 -> 80 per node.

jules: summary so far: kernel compile fallbacks + kv eviction churn -> long token flushes -> p99 spike. Candidate root causes: driver update causing slower kernel JITs; recent workload shape (longer sequences) causing more KV churn.

anand: quick mitigation options: 1) route traffic to older infra pool (pre-driver) 2) pre-warm kernels by running compile jobs 3) purge KV cache to reduce eviction churn (may cause more backend work briefly) 4) enable fail-open slow-mode (return partial tokens quickly)

rachel: let's try 1 + 2 first. route 20% to eu-west-2 (healthy) and kick off a kernel precompile job against hot model variants.

tom: routing change command:
```
rhctl route set traffic --route /v1/stream --from eu-west-1:80% -> eu-west-2:20%
```

tom: routing applied. starting warmup job:
```
rhctl job run --name kernel-warmup --model rwd-chat-1 --regions eu-west-1 --concurrency 4 --duration 120s
```

maya: warmup job started, logs show concurrent compile tasks. watching for reduction in jit failures.

anand: meanwhile I'm checking the driver rollout status; looks like 3/12 nodes have v2.15, scheduled rollout in a maintenance window but somehow drifted. I'll pin those nodes out of rotation temporarily.

jules: how's latency trending?

tom: 3m after mitigations: p95 -> 0.68s, p99 -> 1.9s. token-flush logs show improvement:
```
[INFO] stream: token-flush=320ms, client-wait=410ms
[INFO] gpu-kernel: compile-success, time=180ms
[DEBUG] kvcache: miss-rate lowered 4.5% -> 1.1%
```

jules: good. keep routing at 20% for 10m then ramp down if stable. can we also put a temporary hold on driver rollout and mark nodes for manual review?

anand: done: cordoned 3 nodes and applied hold tag. alerted infra team to investigate the v2.15 regression.

rachel: I'll open an incident ticket and add customer-impact note. support flagged two enterprise customers with noticeable lag for ~8 minutes; noted in support thread.

maya: observed one weirdness: a small subset of streaming sessions show duplicate token gaps after warmup; not consistent. investigating session IDs and trace IDs now.

jules: for immediate next steps:
- anand: infra follow-up to root cause driver regression + rollout gating (TICKET ENG-DRV-992)
- tom: capture and store kernel compile traces and attach to ticket (ENG-RUNTIME-2266)
- maya: session-level anomalies and KV metrics (ENG-OBS-2267)
- rachel: customer comms + incident timeline draft (ENG-COMMS-2268)

rachel: initial incident note: severity=partial-degradation for eu-west-1, impact window ~1766668800-1766669420, mitigation=traffic routing and kernel warmup, customer-visible latency spike, no token loss. will update after 30m watch.

maya: watch period 15m started. metrics stable so far.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status=mitigating, severity=partial-degradation, affected_regions=["eu-west-1"], start_ts=1766668780, mitigation_ts=1766669065, watch=15m

jules: handing off to next oncall @anand for follow-up items and root cause. keep the watch and escalate to oncall-sre if p99 > 3s again.

anand: ack, will pick up postmortem ownership. logging handoff notes in the incident doc. :white_check_mark:
